## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Basal ganglia cell-type map published](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/12/brain-map-basal-ganglia-offers-treatment-clues-parkinsons-schizophrenia/)** — *STAT*
  - A large scientific collaboration released a detailed anatomical and cell-type map of the basal ganglia.
  - The map highlights novel structural and cellular targets for research into psychiatric and neurological conditions, including Parkinson's disease and schizophrenia.

- **[Large-scale GWAS uncovers pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43020908/)** — *PubMed*
  - A genome-wide association study across >1.2 million individuals identified novel genomic loci and pleiotropic pathways underpinning multidimensional pain.

- **[Extracellular human HSP90 extends lifespan and healthspan in *C. elegans*](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.765805)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Exogenous HSP90 delivered via *E. coli* extended the lifespan and healthspan of *C. elegans* without inducing fertility trade-offs.
  - Extracellular HSP90 acts as a signaling ligand activating downstream DAF-16, SKN-1, and HSF-1 transcription factors; combining it with the intracellular senolytic HSP90 inhibitor tanespimycin produced additive longevity benefits.

- **[Caspase-5 couples Cav1.2 cleavage to intestinal barrier dysfunction in colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43020400/)** — *PubMed*
  - Mechanistic work revealed that Caspase-5 couples endosomal Cav1.2-C terminus cleavage to cytosolic LPS release.
  - This pathway directly triggers gut epithelial barrier breakdown during colitis.

- **[CCL17-CCR4 signaling mitigates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.26367804)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Preclinical findings show that CCL17-CCR4 axis activation suppresses IGFBP6 expression in cardiac fibroblasts.
  - This suppression reduces pathological cardiac fibroblast activation and ventricular remodeling during sustained mechanical pressure overload.

- **[Gut microbiome profiles predict long-term MACE risk in prospective European cohorts](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.10.26367787)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Analysis of the FINRISK 2002 cohort with 18-year follow-up identified nine specific gut microbial taxa significantly associated with incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
  - Key microbial features were meta-analyzed and replicated across four independent European validation cohorts (HUNT, HELIUS, SIMPLER, and SCAPIS).

- **[Beat-to-beat blood pressure variability correlates with plasma Alzheimer's biomarkers](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.10.26367476)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Continuous blood pressure monitoring in older adults demonstrated that elevated beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure variability correlates significantly with higher plasma p-Tau217 concentrations ($\beta = 0.32$, $p = 0.003$).

---

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **[Synchron pauses clinical trials for second-generation brain implant](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/health-news-brain-implant-startup-pauses-trials/)** — *STAT*
  - Synchron has placed a temporary pause on clinical trials evaluating its second-generation brain-computer interface (BCI).
  - Executive leadership stated that the pause is operational and not driven by safety concerns.

- **[Systemic and intrathecal alemtuzumab achieves MRD-negative remission in CNS T-PLL](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43021800/)** — *PubMed*
  - Combined systemic and intrathecal administration of the anti-CD52 antibody alemtuzumab induced sustained minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete remission in a patient with T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia (T-PLL) with central nervous system involvement.

- **[HAP-FAST trial evaluates low-dose thoracic CT and rapid sputum PCR in HAP](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.10.26367346)** — *medRxiv*
  - The pilot SMART trial evaluated low-dose thoracic CT imaging alongside BioFire FilmArray Pneumonia Plus rapid molecular sputum testing prior to second antibiotic dosing in adults with non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia.

---

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[EMPIRICAL trial: Empirical TB treatment fails to improve survival in HIV-positive infant pneumonia](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01418-2/fulltext?rss=yes)** — *The Lancet*
  - A multicenter, open-label $2 \times 2$ factorial Phase 3 trial in African infants hospitalized with HIV-associated severe pneumonia showed that empirical anti-tuberculosis therapy (eTB-T) did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality compared to a pathogen-guided strategy.
  - Frequent initiation of targeted TB treatment during follow-up in the control arm likely narrowed the outcome gap between arms.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Upadacitinib demonstrates sustained 48-week efficacy in juvenile idiopathic arthritis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43021638/)** — *PubMed*
  - 48-week readouts from the SELECT-YOUTH open-label extension study confirmed long-term safety and disease control for AbbVie's JAK inhibitor upadacitinib in patients with polyarticular-course juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Aztreonam-avibactam evaluated in critically ill patients with resistant Gram-negative infections](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43020993/)** — *PubMed*
  - A Phase 3 REVISIT trial subgroup analysis evaluated Pfizer and AbbVie's aztreonam-avibactam versus colistin plus meropenem in critically ill patients with severe Gram-negative bacterial infections.

- **[Intensive blood pressure control preserves cognitive function in type 2 diabetes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43020520/)** — *PubMed*
  - Prespecified secondary analyses of the randomized BPROAD trial showed that intensive blood pressure control yields structural brain preservation and reduces cognitive decline in adults with type 2 diabetes.

- **[GVHD prophylaxis regimens differentially alter gut microbiome recovery](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43020901/)** — *PubMed*
  - A Phase 3 microbiome substudy revealed that standard graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis regimens exert distinct effects on gut microbiome diversity and reconstitution kinetics following allogeneic stem cell transplantation.

---

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma]** **[FDA grants accelerated approval to ponatinib with chemotherapy for newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-ponatinib-chemotherapy-newly-diagnosed-philadelphia-chromosome)** — *FDA*
  - The FDA granted accelerated approval to ponatinib (Iclusig, Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc.) in combination with chemotherapy for adult patients with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL).
  - Efficacy was evaluated in the Phase 3 PhALLCON trial (NCT03589326), a randomized 2:1 open-label trial comparing ponatinib (30 mg once daily) against imatinib (600 mg once daily) alongside induction and consolidation chemotherapy.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[FDA grants accelerated approval to repotrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-repotrectinib-adult-and-pediatric-patients-ntrk-gene-fusion-positive)** — *FDA*
  - The FDA granted accelerated approval to repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol-Myers Squibb) for adult and pediatric patients aged $\ge$12 years with locally advanced or metastatic NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumors following progression on prior therapy or without satisfactory alternatives.
  - Approval was supported by data from the multicenter, single-arm TRIDENT-1 trial (NCT03093116) across TKI-pretreated and TKI-naïve cohorts.

- **[FDA finalizes ICH M15 guidance on model-informed drug development](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/webinar-stakeholder-engagement-new-final-guideline-general-principles-model-informed-drug)** — *FDA*
  - The FDA implemented the finalized ICH M15 guideline, establishing global regulatory standards for planning, evaluating, and documenting evidence derived from model-informed drug development (MIDD).

- **[Big Pharma]** **[FDA outlines updates on accelerated approvals and indication withdrawals](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-sacituzumab-govitecan-advanced-urothelial-cancer)** — *FDA*
  - The FDA completed the final withdrawal of Gilead's sacituzumab govitecan-hziy (Trodelvy) for second-line metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
  - Broader guidance updates highlight prior accelerated approvals, including Jazz Pharmaceuticals' zanidatamab-hrii (Ziihera) with Roche's VENTANA 4B5 companion diagnostic for HER2+ biliary tract cancer, and Amgen's tarlatamab-dlle (Imdelltra) for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.

- **[Game Changer Products issues recall for undeclared prescription ingredients](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/game-changer-products-llc-issues-voluntary-nationwide-recall-10-day-forecast-capsules-due-presence)** — *FDA*
  - Game Changer Products voluntarily recalled all lots of 10 Day Forecast 3200mg capsules after FDA testing confirmed contamination with undeclared sildenafil and acetaminophen.

---

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Blackstone commits $1.5B to back Pfizer’s monthly obesity candidate](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/12/biotech-news-blackstone-backs-pfizer-bet-on-monthly-obesity-treatment/)** — *STAT*
  - Private equity firm Blackstone is investing up to $1.5 billion to fund Phase 3 development of Pfizer's berobenatide, a monthly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist acquired via Metsera.
  - The co-funding arrangement allows Pfizer to offset late-stage clinical trial expenditures while retaining commercialization rights.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Eli Lilly faces conflict-of-interest questions over Oura telehealth deal](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/oura-acquisition-counsel-health-eli-lilly/)** — *STAT*
  - Smart-ring company Oura's acquisition of telehealth startup Counsel Health has raised ethical and conflict-of-interest scrutiny regarding Eli Lilly's ownership stakes and commercial relationships with telehealth platforms marketing GLP-1 drugs.

- **[Biotech]** **[Windward prices $175M IPO alongside $50M Sanofi private placement](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/windward-ipo-pricing-immune-drugs-china-deals-tezspire/874533/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Swiss biotech Windward priced a $175 million IPO and secured an additional $50 million private placement investment from **[Big Pharma]** Sanofi.
  - Capital will advance clinical development of China-licensed respiratory therapeutics aimed at competing with AstraZeneca and Amgen's TSLP inhibitor Tezspire.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Bristol Myers Squibb merges R&D operations; Chief Scientific Officer departs](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bristol-myers-robert-plenge-cristian-massacesi-research-transition/874476/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - BMS Head of Research Robert Plenge is departing as the company merges its early research and clinical development divisions into a single unified R&D organization.

- **[Venture capital interest rebounds in neuroscience biotechs](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/charts-venture-neuroscience-oyster-vectory-acr-cell-therapy/874570/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Five early-stage neurology biotechs collected approximately $450 million in venture funding over recent weeks, signaling renewed investor demand for CNS therapeutics relative to cell therapy programs.

---

## Public Health & Policy

- **[US Senators introduce bill targeting financial conflicts on USPSTF panel](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/uspstf-preventive-care-panel-senators-target-conflicts-of-interest/)** — *STAT*
  - U.S. Senators introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at restricting financial conflicts of interest among members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF).

- **[Global fertility tourism clinics market unproven 'three-parent IVF'](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/fertility-tourism-5-takeaways-mrt-investigation/)** — *STAT*
  - A STAT investigation revealed that international fertility clinics are commercially offering unproven mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT) to older women without established regulatory oversight or clinical efficacy data.

- **[ENSO climate cycles linked to severe African cholera surges](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.26367838)** — *medRxiv*
  - Epidemiological modeling across 30 African countries demonstrated strong teleconnections between El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phases and localized cholera outbreaks.
  - Models project a 2- to 5-fold increase in cholera burden in East Africa for the 2026–2027 El Niño cycle compared to neutral baseline conditions.

- **[FDA warns against unapproved joint pain products containing hidden active ingredients](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/medication-health-fraud-notifications/yuan-bone-may-be-harmful-due-hidden-ingredients)** — *FDA*
  - The FDA issued public notifications advising consumers against purchasing or using "Yuan Bone" and "Ismerely Mire-X," products marketed online and in retail stores for joint pain.
  - Laboratory testing identified unlabelled acetaminophen, chlorpheniramine, and diclofenac in Yuan Bone, and undeclared diclofenac and dexamethasone in Ismerely Mire-X.
  - The hidden ingredients present severe risks of hepatotoxicity, immunosuppression, and cardiovascular/gastrointestinal toxicities.

---

**Worth watching:** Blackstone’s novel $1.5 billion risk-sharing investment structure for Pfizer’s monthly GLP-1 candidate (berobenatide) signals a potential paradigm shift in how Big Pharma offloads Phase 3 development costs in capital-intensive indications.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Why Walmart's New Healthcare Strategy Might Work](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Ks11EGHE4Fw) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Malak Atut discusses healthcare strategy and the role of domain expertise in healthtech ventures.
        - Partnering with subject matter experts can significantly improve a healthcare company's probability of success.
        - Strategic expert partnerships provide structural advantages even when companies cannot directly control final patient outcomes.
    - [Your Company Was Never Meant to Need You Forever](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/L8Y7x9-ndJ0) -- Health2Tech
        - Alison Curfman highlights the importance of organizational design and leadership scalability in startups.
        - Successful founders prioritize building strong, capable teams to manage operations and strategic execution.
        - Sustainable company growth requires creating organizational systems that function independently of the original founder's direct oversight.
    - [The Startup Playbook Is Broken. Here's What Comes Next | Bret Waters](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v3uX02wf2do) -- Health2Tech
        - Artificial intelligence is altering startup economics, enabling lean three-person teams to achieve output that previously required thirty employees.
        - Proprietary software is no longer a durable competitive moat, shifting strategic advantage toward vertical AI, industry-specific execution, and founder-driven capabilities.
        - Venture capital fundraising alone does not ensure success, favoring strategies grounded in the "Adjacent Possible" framework and a "Fail, Fast, Forward" iteration philosophy.
        - Digital health founders face distinct commercialization obstacles due to long sales cycles and complex purchasing decisions, demanding deliberate metrics for pivoting versus persevering.
- Pure Science
    - [Making Gunpowder From Scratch](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/V8rT6UI3Crg) -- Veritasium
        - The historical formulation of early gunpowder relies on a mixture of three natural chemical ingredients.
        - The chemical preparation and demonstration were conducted in a controlled environment by qualified professionals.
        - Safety disclaimers explicitly warn viewers against attempting to manufacture gunpowder independently.
    - [Plato Got Vision Totally Wrong](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5qYRfCnIITk) -- minutephysics
        - Historical theories of perception, such as Plato's "visual fire," incorrectly posited that eyes emit light rays to sense external objects.
        - Physicist Ibn al-Haytham disproved emission theories by establishing that vision functions through rays of light entering the eye from external sources.
        - Johannes Kepler expanded on optical physics and biological mechanics by detailing how the physical lens of the eye refractorily focuses light.
    - [How Do You Take a Picture of a Black Hole? | PODCAST: The Joy of Why](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qzIt6uCFfu8) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Astrophysicist Shep Doeleman explains how the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) linked global radio telescopes together to effectively synthesize an Earth-sized telescope.
        - The EHT captured the first images of supermassive black hole shadows, targeting M87—located 55 million light-years away—and Sagittarius A* at the center of the Milky Way.
        - The observed ring-like structures surrounding black hole shadows allow scientists to test theoretical predictions of general relativity against alternative physical models.
        - The EHT collaboration aims to advance from static imaging to creating dynamic movies of black holes by the early 2030s to study how their environments evolve over time.
- Other
    - [How Humans Changed the Earth: Crash Course Geology #24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GJrG2AxmD3g) -- CrashCourse
        - Examines the concept of the Anthropocene, a proposed geological epoch defined by widespread and potentially irreversible human impacts on Earth.
        - Highlights novel geological markers of human activity, such as "plastic rocks" formed by synthetic debris integrating into the rock record.
        - Discusses the ongoing debate among geologists regarding whether human influence currently meets the formal criteria for a new designated epoch.
        - Explores potential methods and challenges for humans to adapt to or reverse systemic environmental and geological changes.
- To watch
    - [Working on something new...](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/x6bmBlZKFw4) -- Domain of Science
